# Integrator class

Runtime and reporting implementors exhaustively render these host-policy
outcomes; provider adapters never construct them.

oneOf.description: Host policy requires a provider idempotency or resume guarantee.
The per-call unsafe retry allowance is exhausted.
Provider-reported tokens exceed the host's duplicate-cost bound.

EffectAddress.description: Canonical address of one admitted runtime effect.

ExecCodeFailureReason.description:
Why an `exec_code` effect failed before the executor produced a response.

This is the closed classification offline trace analysis keys on; the human
detail lives in [`ExecCodeFailure::message`]. Serialized snake_case on the
durable journal and trace surfaces.

oneOf.description: No code executor is installed on the session.
The executor's language runtime exited unexpectedly.
Any other session-layer failure; `message` carries the detail.

A journal entry written before the reason was typed: only the human
message survived the erasure, so no closed reason can be recovered.

ExecutionNodeKind.description:
Closed vocabulary of executable workflow sites.

This describes the site, not its current observation. A workflow node may
expose more than one site kind. Declaration order is the canonical order:
a node's execution sites sort by it, so reordering the variants changes
the serialized workflow graph and needs a graph schema bump.

ExecutionScope.description:
Stable semantic identity for one effectful runtime operation.

This is the scope admitted by the host boundary before nondeterministic
work begins. Its journal encoding is an existing durable contract; effect
addresses compose it with a replay key without changing those bytes.

oneOf.description:
One operation on a session that runs no turn: a host command, named
by its batch, or the admissions of one shift request. It has no
logical root, and no logical turn runs under it.

GenerationOptionOutcome.description:
What became of one host-set generation setting on one request.

A setting a host sets is sent, or the call is refused before any I/O with a
typed failure; nothing is silently dropped. The receipt therefore names only
the two deliberate non-send dispositions besides `Applied`: a cap reduced to
the model's capacity, and stop sequences a protocol owns. `Applied` means
lash put the value on the wire, never that the provider complied.

oneOf.description: The host expressed no preference, so there was nothing to apply.
The host asked for it and the request carries it.

A protocol suppressed the caller's non-empty stop list because its
grammar owns the response boundary. This is intentional protocol
ownership, but the caller's requested value did not reach the wire.

Explicit prompt-cache breakpoints the protocol placed that this
adapter's wire has no cache directive for. Only the `cache` row, which
reports protocol-placed breakpoints rather than a host setting, uses it.

The caller asked for an output-token cap above what this model can
produce, and the request carries the model's capacity instead. The
bound the caller asked for still holds; the number on the wire is
smaller than the one they named.

GenerationReceipt.description:
Per-call account of every host generation setting: resolution supplies
what was requested, the adapter supplies what it emitted.

This is request-side, adapter-owned bookkeeping and deliberately separate
from [`ExecutionEvidence`], which carries only facts the provider reported
about the execution.

cache.description: Fate of explicit prompt-cache breakpoints in the request.

output_token_cap.description: The effective cap: the request's, else the provider options'.

reasoning.description: The model spec's reasoning selection; `ProviderDefault` is not a request.

reasoning_retention.description: The model spec's reasoning-history retention selection.

thinking_summary.description:
`expose_thinking`'s wire half: a reasoning summary requested from the
provider.

thinking_visibility.description: `expose_thinking`'s local half: reasoning output published to the host.

GroupWakePolicy.description:
Aggregate wake rule. Run-owned aggregates preserve these semantics;
the rule does not require a durable group dispatcher.

`Promise.all` and `Promise.allSettled` both use [`All`](Self::All): the
caller's early exit on rejection is not a host wake rule. The wire shape
has no default, so a missing rule cannot be replayed under a guess.

oneOf.description: Wake on the first settlement of any kind.
Wake on the first success, or after every child fails.
Deliver every settlement in durable rank order.

MaxToolCalls.description:
The number of tool calls one execution may make: the host's required
decision, with no default and no built-in ceiling (FIG-4546).

What it counts depends on the execution. A cell — one code cell of a turn,
or one tool step of a protocol without cells — may make at most this many
tool calls in total. A process may hold at most this many at once: a call
counts from its acceptance until the process no longer depends on it, so
a long-running process is bounded in what it retains, never in what it
does over its life. The call that passes the limit fails with
[`ToolCallLimitExceeded`]; every call under it runs untouched. The limit
paces nothing: rate limits and throttling are the host's own.

NormalizedError.description: A journal-safe projection of a provider/transport failure.

code.description:
The failure code, namespaced by who authored the spelling: `lash:` for
workspace-authored codes, `provider:` for provider wire vocabulary,
and a host's own namespace for host-authored codes.

ProviderFailureKind.description:
Classification of a provider/transport failure.

This is the single canonical failure-kind vocabulary: provider transports
classify failures into it (`lash-core` re-exports it from
`llm::transport`), the turn machine carries it on
[`ErrorEnvelope`](crate::session_model::ErrorEnvelope), and hosts read it
back from `TurnIssue`s without scraping traces.

`Unknown` is an explicit classification, never a decoder fallback.
Persisted failure records reject unrecognized kind literals.

RemoteProcessDurableCompleteness.description: Durable-summary completeness, reported apart from live-graph completeness.

RemoteProcessDurableGapReason.description: Why a durable summary fold is not the whole history through its boundary.

oneOf.description: Bounded acquisition stopped before the high-water mark.
A summary event in the history did not decode.

The host released a prefix of the history; the summary folds only
the events after it.

RemoteProcessDurableSnapshot.description:
The durable half of a snapshot: status and the effect-summary fold
through one exact high-water sequence, or why there is none.

RemoteProcessEffectNodeReport.description: One effect node's recorded occurrences and omitted counts.

RemoteProcessEffectOccurrence.description: One recorded effect occurrence in a durable summary.

RemoteProcessEffectOmittedCounts.description: Omitted occurrences of one node, by outcome class.

RemoteProcessHistoryRetention.description: Why the exact lifetime a snapshot names has no durable history to read.

oneOf.description: The process was pruned and its payload-free tombstone remains.
No retained process or tombstone has this id.

RemoteProcessObservationCompleteness.description: Live-graph completeness, reported apart from durable-summary completeness.

oneOf.description:
Retained live evidence cannot bridge the cursor's durable sequence to
the durable high-water mark.
The requested process lifetime is unknown or no longer retained.

RemoteProcessObservationProjection.description:
The live half of a snapshot: the publisher's graph, when this core routes
the process.

RemoteProcessObservationSnapshot.description:
A snapshot at one exact process lifetime and durable high-water sequence,
with the live graph at the cursor's live position.

oneOf.description:
Mirrors [`lash_core::ProcessStatus::CallerDeparted`]: durably
distinguishable, deliberately never terminal.

RemoteRetiredProcessStatus.description:
Mirrors [`lash_core::RetiredProcessStatus`]: the status a pruned process
ended in, which its tombstone keeps.

RetryClass.description: Evidence that permits another provider attempt.

ToolCallLimitExceeded.description:
A tool call refused by the session's [`MaxToolCalls`]: the program asked
for more tool calls than its recorded limit admits.

It is the program's failure, never the host's: the limit is recorded
config and the count is a fact of the program's own history, so a replay
or a redrive refuses the same call. Nothing of the refused calls is
journaled or dispatched.

counted.description:
The calls counted against the limit before the refused ones: made so
far by a cell, held now by a process.

limit.description: The recorded `max_tool_calls` the execution runs under.

requested.description:
The calls refused together: one for a single call, an aggregate's
unique tool calls for an aggregate.

oneOf.description: A cell: the limit is the total it may make.
A process: the limit is what it may hold at once.

TraceAttemptUsageOutcome.description:
Why an attempt's provider-reported usage is present or absent.

Mirrors `lash_sansio::llm::types::AttemptUsageOutcome`, the vocabulary's
owner, with the same wire spellings; the trace layer was the only one that
flattened it to a free-form string.

# Integrator class

Reporting integrations exhaustively render these outcomes when
explaining a call whose usage never arrived.

oneOf.description: The provider reported usage for this attempt.
The provider completed the attempt without reporting usage.
The attempt was aborted before usage could be collected.
The attempt failed before usage could be collected.

graph_node_id.description:
Stable id of the span this record represents (e.g. `turn:<session>:<turn>`,
`llm:<call_id>`, `tool:<call_id>`). Populated by the runtime for turn /
llm / tool / session records so a consumer can build a nested span tree
from `(graph_node_id, parent_graph_node_id)` with a single `id -> span`
map. A language-execution record for a node event carries the observed
node's structural id here, equal to the `WorkflowGraph` node id (ADR
0100 R0), so a host joins trace to graph on this key; a child start
carries its parent node's id, and execution start and finish leave it
unset.

parent_graph_node_id.description:
Id of the enclosing span — the value of some other record's
`graph_node_id`. A turn's parent is its causal origin (the spawning tool
call / effect, via `caused_by`) when known, otherwise the session root.

TraceDurableWaitResolution.description: How a durable wait left its park.

The awaited event delivered a host-domain error value.
The wait itself was cancelled.

TraceEffectEnvelopeDiffEvent.description:
Structural differences between the canonical envelopes on a failed durable
replay validation. This event may contain prompt and tool-result values and
must therefore only be emitted through the extended-trace gate.

TraceEffectEnvelopeDiffValue.description:
One side of a divergent canonical-envelope value.

Large values are omitted whole. Their exact serialized length and digest
remain available, but no prefix is retained.

TraceJournaledEffectStatus.description: Terminal status of a journaled `ctx.run` effect.

oneOf.description:
The named occurrence has parked on an observed wait. Its `since` is
the enclosing trace record timestamp, not a separately sampled clock.

A parked occurrence resolved, including cancellation. Its node terminal
remains a separate fact.
Only an occurrence observed in flight may be cancelled.

TraceLanguageExecutionFailure.description: The observed cause of a failed language node.

oneOf.description:
A dispatched tool effect failed with its recorded classification and
recorded source and retry status. `replay_key` is the causing effect's identity.
A VM or host-boundary failure with a stable runtime error code.

TraceLanguageExecutionMap.description:
The static graph of an execution, carried once on
[`TraceLanguageExecutionPayload::ExecutionStarted`]. Identity
(`module_ref`, `entry_kind`, `entry_ref`, `entry_name`) lives solely on the
enclosing [`TraceLanguageExecutionIdentity`]; the map never restates it.

branch_memberships.description: Observed branch selections that admit this node's arm.

TraceLashlangEdgeSelection.description:
Observed branch-edge selection state.

Only the edge a `BranchSelected` event names is marked. There is no
`Rejected`: the execution map carries data-dependency and sequencing edges
(ADR 0037) and nothing marks an edge as a branch arm, so an unselected arm
is indistinguishable from an ordinary edge leaving the same node. Which arm
ran is read from the typed selection on the branch node itself
([`TraceLashlangGraphNode::branch_selection`]).

TraceLashlangEventIdentity.description:
Canonical identity of one fold input.

Node transitions use `(node_id, node_kind, occurrence, attempt)` plus
the transition kind. The transition kind lets a start and its terminal
fact merge monotonically while still making a second, different start or
terminal a typed conflict.

TraceLashlangGraph.description: Trace-derived Lashlang execution graph snapshot for hosts and debugging tools.

TraceLashlangGraphChildLink.description: Link from an observed parent Lashlang node to a child execution graph.

TraceLashlangGraphCompleteness.description: Whether the static execution map was available to the fold.

TraceLashlangGraphConflict.description: A bounded, typed record of divergent values under one logical identity.

TraceLashlangGraphConflictKind.description: Why two records under one logical identity did not deduplicate.

TraceLashlangGraphHistoryEvent.description: One canonical event retained so a persisted snapshot can be folded again.

branch_selection.description:
Which arm a branch node took, copied from the typed `selected` field of
the `BranchSelected` event. Absent on every other node, and on a branch
whose selection has not been observed yet.

TraceLashlangNodeRetention.description: Aggregate facts for occurrences evicted from one node's bounded history.

usage.description: Provider-reported usage only. Absence is not zero usage.

generation_disposition.description:

request_model.description: The model identifier requested for the corresponding LLM call.

TraceProviderReplayKind.description:
Opaque replay state rejected before an LLM Provider request was serialized.
A missing minting route identifies a session written before provenance was

body_json_omitted_reason.description: Why `body_json` is absent when the request body itself was observed.

body_sha256.description:
SHA-256 of the exact serialized wire bytes. `body_json` is a parsed

TraceRecord.description:
One durable trace record: the envelope fields plus the flattened

oneOf.description: One attachment was omitted so an otherwise valid session can continue.

Complete model-facing composition captured only when its fingerprint

Full model-facing tool contracts in request order. This is kept

oneOf.description:
One real provider request attempt of a model call, made by the body

The terminal of a durable domain operation that has no record of its

provider_call_id.description: The model provider's id for the call, when a model issued it.

oneOf.description:
A logical receipt from recorded Run events. A final is observed only
after its protected presentation; a Deferred attempt has no terminal.

provider_call_id.description: The model provider's id for the call, when a model issued it.

error.description: Human-readable detail. Not a stable classification surface.

reason.description:
Closed failure classification; offline analysis keys on this rather

oneOf.description:
A journaled effect is about to cross its durable substrate's journal
command boundary.
A journaled effect returned its recorded or newly executed outcome.
A durable wait has issued its park command.

A durable timer has been issued.

Compile/link evidence a protocol plugin reports before it executes a

TraceTurnCancellationEvidence.description:
Durable evidence that the traced turn was cancelled. Mirrors the runtime's

[`TurnStop::Cancelled`]: lash_sansio::session_model::TurnStop::Cancelled

origin.description: Opaque host-domain data. Lash records and returns it unchanged.

TraceTurnFailureReason.description:
Why a [`TraceTurnOutcome::Failed`] turn stopped. Mirrors the non-cancelled

TraceTurnOutcome.description:
The single terminal outcome of a traced turn.

One closed shape replaces the former `status` / `done_reason` /
`agent_frame_switch` triple: each variant owns exactly the data its state
can carry, so an agent-frame switch cannot be reported without a frame key
and a cancellation cannot be reported without its evidence. Cancellation is
its own variant rather than a failure reason — [`Self::is_failed`] is
`false` for it.

oneOf.description: The turn reached a terminal result the caller asked for.
The turn ended by handing control to another agent frame.

The turn ended at a segment boundary of its run, which goes on in a
new invocation. `done_reason` is why: `journal_budget` or `hand_over`.
The turn was cancelled. Not a failure.
The turn stopped short of a result.

WorkerFrameKind.description: The worker message an encoder refused, without its guest data.

oneOf.description:
A step's execution observations outgrew the run's heap budget, which

The encoded effect request or result exceeds its configured bound.
A snapshot or continuation exceeds its configured bound.
A worker message cannot fit in one transport frame.
